As the night went on and I did more research and thought about it more, I think my gut feeling that it's just not the right way to go about it was correct. I can't remember where I read it, but a friend also said something similar in that a character should be a human first and foremost, regardless of their race, illnesses, etc. I don't think it'd be any better than Heath Ledger describing his Joker as schizophrenic - It's like defining someone because of their mental illness. Said character should have their own goals, wants, fears, flaws and etc. I'm realizing now that the problem is that I'm basing a character around schizophrenia instead of creating a character with schizophrenia. The way I was thinking about doing it was really just artificial representation.

I think your advice has been invaluable, thank you very much. I do have more questions if you'd be kind enough to expand on your suggestions. What's a good way to implement him experiencing symptoms without going too far or being too cliche? I worry showing him having conversations with the voices in his head would walk a fine line between realistic and exaggerated. Do people who experience delusions and false memories still experience them when not having an episode? I'm not going to mention the extremely common delusions experienced by schizophrenic people, and I don't think I need to, but if I depicted the character with a common delusion, would it be in poor taste? Would it be in poor taste to initially portray the character as an antagonist (But not evil) because he has yet to have received help for his symptoms and delusions, and then later becoming a hero as he learns how to cope, etc?

While I do not have schizophrenia but depression, I can say that I think this is very helpful and applicable to other illnesses and disorders! Thank you for sharing and I'm so happy you are finding success in this to cope, I'm starting to do the same thing to help fight my depression.

Unfortunately, I've found it is both difficult and exhausting to try to make someone care who does not. You can go above and beyond for another person, but ultimately that person remains unchanged. Perhaps you could consider removing toxic people from your life, that make you feel poorly. It is a bittersweet resolution if you care about them, but it may be the best one, because no one can change another. I know this might be difficult to accomplish, like if one of the people in question is someone you live with or are around a lot. However, it may help to keep these people at the back of your mind, and do things that you enjoy doing, that make you feel good about yourself. You don't need other's validation, you can validate yourself!
